en: The Ritual Scripture of the Greatly Majestic and Wrathful Ucchuṣma.
By [the monk] Grand Master of the Palace with the Rank of Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sushun Commandery with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, Invested with Purple Robes, and Posthumously Honored as Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
All Buddhas of the ten directions, Possessors of wondrous wisdom who rescue through compassion,
Who eternally abide in the bodhicitta— Therefore, I prostrate to Samantabhadra,
Who is the very essence of all Buddhas, The one who receives the office and holds the vajra.
To subdue those who are difficult to tame, this embodiment of the Vidyārāja is manifested;
because its method is supreme, the practitioner of mantras should first practice the preliminary service (pūrvasevā), whether in pure or impure states.
Use red sandalwood to smear the ground, forming it into a square or circle as desired.
Based upon that, in the eastern direction, place the image of the primary deity and take two *argha* vessels, filling them with scented water.
Burn various incenses in the incense burner; place an empty vessel filled with water within the altar area.
Whether one eats or does not eat, one should likewise rinse both mouth and hands.
Then, prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground in salutation.
To the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, In this Vaipulya Mahāyāna Sūtra,
With palms joined and a sincere heart, One should place the right knee upon the ground.
The non-virtuous karma accumulated over many lifetimes Is a mass of transgressions too vast to describe in full.
Now, with a sincere heart, perform the confession according to the vow for purification;
having made the aspiration as before, sit in the full-lotus or half-lotus posture and give rise to the great bodhicitta,
remaining firm and never abandoning it at any time.
For the mudrā of applying fragrant incense to the hands: join the two palms with the hollowed fingers of the Buddha-family samaya;
extend the index and middle fingers slightly bent, and press the tips of the ring and little fingers against the first joints of the thumbs, with the backs of the thumbs meeting at the first phalanx.
Furthermore, bend the heads of the wisdom-fingers (middle fingers) and place them at the side of the first joint of the advancing-force fingers (index fingers).
With this mudrā held at the heart, contemplate the appearance of the Tathāgata with focused attention. The mantra for the gate is as follows:
Having recited the dhāraṇī three times, the light of all Tathāgatas awakens and pervasively touches the body;
karma is eliminated and afflictions are extinguished.
Afterwards, one should place it upon the crown of the head; by performing the mudrā of scattering, empowerment is accomplished.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā within the Lotus:
join the two hands as before; extend the fingers of the *śīla*, *kṣānti*, and *praṇidhāna* [fingers], and likewise the *vīrya* and *bala* [fingers].
If one spreads out the eight petals of the lotus:
Place the seal of peace upon the heart; visualize the Honored One Avalokiteśvara complete according to the original ritual procedure.
Recite the dhāraṇī three times to awaken the Lotus Family; may the assembly of sages emit radiant light.
Illuminating and touching the body of the practitioner, The obstacles are dissolved and they become my friends.
Place the seal upon the right side of the crown, And then disperse it as you wish.
Then bind the Vajra Armor, The Samaya Secret Seal.
Having spread its two wings, the right is raised upward and the left is turned downward,
with their backs joined together. The *tāṇḍava* hook is formed by the *prajñāpāramitā* and *prajñā*,
further bound with *dhyāna*, like a ten-pronged vajra.
Visualize [the deity] within the heart; recite the mantra while contemplating the Lord of the Family and awakening the assembly of Vajras.
May the Noble One emit light that touches the practitioner, bestowing blessings as a spiritual friend.
For the *mūrdha-vāmā-vikṣepa-mudrā*: Interlace the two palms with the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers forming a peak;
slightly bend the *madhyamā* and *kaniṣṭhā* fingers so they each rest against the side of the central peak, and extend the *tarjanī* and *jyeṣṭhā* fingers together.
Having completed the three-pronged practice, form the mudrā at the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, and likewise at the heart; thereafter, apply it to the throat.
Once the mudrā is formed, the body is protected; recite the subsequent mantra for all.
His majestic radiance blazes intensely, such that the hosts of Māra cannot invade him.
Both hands form hollow fists; the fingers other than those held by the Dhyāna and Prajñā mudrās are joined.
The right hand is opened and grasps the left; the fingers of the "crossing over" (pāramitā) mudrā stand straight like mountain peaks.
Raising the mudrā at the head, recite the Great Heart Mantra three times.
Having completed this, join the hands as for the principal deity,
bend the tips of the fingers forward so that the peaks meet, insert them into the palms, and extend the thumbs.
Recite this three times. The mudrās for the crowns of the deities are the same as the two previously mentioned;
by bending the index and middle fingers and joining them in the shape of a ring, one forms the armor for the five locations.
Interlace the two wings within; open the palms and extend them all wide.
Join the *aṅguṣṭha* (thumb) and *prajñā* (little finger) to form a peak. Slightly bend the joints of the *dhyāna* (ring finger) and *jñāna* (middle finger), leaving them half-bent.
Shift the *vīrya* (index finger) and *bala* (forefinger) slightly toward the side. Extend them widely and straighten them to form the "Universal Flame" (*Samantaprabhā*).
Recite the mantra of the Great Mind (*mahācitta-mantra*) three times while placing the mudrā at the chest.
Recite the vidyā-phrase three times; let the mind become one with the deity.
Change the *kavaca* (armor) and advance the *vajra-bandha* (diamond-binding); extend them fully so that their respective characteristics merge.
As for the needle, it is called the "Holding Seal" (*dhāraṇī-mudrā*).
After reciting its subsequent mantra, one further displays the *Samantaprabhā* seal. The *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers form the shape of a needle;
this root mantra is named the "Single-pronged Vajra."
The body of the *iṣṭadevatā* (the deity) enters [the site] as the very essence of great power;
because it firmly maintains that ground, one should likewise employ the vajrakīla between the precepts (*śīla*),
liberative means (*upāya*), and wisdom (*prajñā*), while also bending with the power of aspiration (*praṇidhāna*).
Furthermore, one enters into generosity and ethical discipline; may one abide within patience and diligence, while the remaining perfections are all extended straight.
These features combine to form three prongs, using meditative concentration and wisdom as pillars for the ground. One pull and one invocation clarify this.
Oṃ kili kili.
From here down to the vajra-wheel, it is firm and indestructible;
following the previous method, take the ritual stake as the basis, and fully open the dhyāna-jñāna-pāramitā.
The syllable *ṭha* is formed directly from *ja*.
Recite the vidyā three times while clearly visualizing the ground where you dwell.
After reciting the mantra that produces the transparent great ocean, it shall be accomplished upon seven recitations.
Next, one should visualize that from the ocean a great Mount Sumeru surges forth;
then recite this mantra seven times before ceasing.
Furthermore, one should again visualize the lion throne adorned upon the mountain of jewels.
Its brilliance is as described below;

likewise, for seven repetitions, he rests upon the lion-dharma throne, where a hundred-leafed, thousand-petaled precious lotus—fragrant, pure, and magnificent—is fully blossomed. Recite this secret mantra:
Within that lotus pedestal, a pavilion is formed of various jewels,
hung with exquisite silk banners and draped with nets of *kiṅkiṇī*.
Recite the mantra as follows seven times, visualizing its accomplishment accordingly.
Next, again holding an incense burner, recite the Mantra for Purifying the Path:
"The pivotal bolts within the void / And all obstacles are entirely removed.
Next, bind the Seal of the Precious Chariot to invite and welcome the various holy ones.
Having single-handedly invited [the deity] together with their retinue according to one’s wish, the two wings (index fingers) should be crossed inward.
The thumbs and forefingers are extended and pressed against each other;
the wisdom finger (ring finger) and the effort finger (middle finger) pinch the first joint of the effort finger. This is the first mudrā of the Root [Mantra].
The wrists should be fully opened, with the backs of the fingers touching the palms;
recite the mantra three times. The seven-jeweled carriage is completed;
when the visualization reaches the stage of the Principal Deity, [recite] *Aṇakavati*.
Having visualized the ceremonial carriage, one should next perform the invitation according to the previous ritual for the precious carriage.
With the fingers of the patience-vow and meditation-wisdom mudrās turned inward, form the seal of invitation. Recite the mantra as follows:
The Noble One ascends the precious chariot; With the Vajra as the driver, he shall arrive.
One should then invoke him with the mudrā of the Family Lord to descend into the maṇḍala.
Crossing the two hands inwardly, place the dhyāna fingers between the prajñā fingers.
Forming a fist, raise the Prajñāpāramitā finger; each time you beckon, recite the mantra and offer it according to the seal.
Next, extend the Kṣānti and Varada fingers, joining them with the Vīrya and Bala fingers; place the right hand above and cross them.
Slowly move the thighs; the mantra syllables for eliminating all obstacles follow as below.
Perform three clockwise circumambulations simultaneously, then form the Vajrapāśa mudrā by placing the thumbs beneath the ring fingers.
Wisdom is also empowered by force; the first text for the mantra at the side of the faculties is as follows:
"Recite the mantra as it appears below.
To cover the wall with a net, form the seal of the dense suture for the great courtyard: extend both hands together."
Empowered with the wings of concentration and wisdom, straight and firm,
having performed three circumambulations to the right through dhyāna and prajñāpāramitā, one recites the subsequent mantra;
the vajra wall stands surrounding it, blazing with fierce flames.
Once the firm element has been established, nothing shall be able to obstruct or destroy it.
One should place the right knee upon the ground,
hold the vessel of *argha* water level with the forehead, and recite the Great Heart Mantra.
Diligently hold and offer this; may it fulfill the heart’s desired wishes for bathing the feet of the assembly of noble ones.
Herein, one should fully present [the offering];
let the subtle vessel sink into emptiness, and place the water in its original position.
As previously described for the Lotus Family,
one should form that samaya mudrā by hooking the tips of the six fingers;
visualizing them in the posture of a slightly blooming lotus as vajra petals, one recites the mantra three times.
As previously visualized, the assembly of sages is solemnly seated in their proper order.
One should then perform offerings from the heart, including all flowers found on land and water that are not owned by anyone,
throughout the entirety of the void of the ten directions.
Human and celestial unguents and the like, incense, lamps, empty canopies, umbrellas, and banners;
drums, music, song, dance, and performers;
exquisite nets of pearls, and various jeweled bells suspended [therein].
White whisks and flower garlands, Scattered wonderful incense and flowers,
A net of *kiṅkiṇī* bells, And the king of wish-fulfilling jewel trees;
Next, one partakes of celestial kitchen-clouds, Exquisite, beautiful, fragrant, and pure.
With clouds of offerings such as pavilions adorned with jewels,
celestial garlands, and crowns, filling the entire realm of space,
one should contemplate with a sincere heart; furthermore, by means of mudrās and mantras.
Sustained by the power of the Sage, the treasury of space provides for all the noble ones to enjoy; it is truly without distinction.
The ten perfections are mutually interwoven: with the right hand pressing down upon the left, join the palms.
Raising the mudrā to the crown of the head,
recite the Ghaṇṭā-paṭala mantra followed by melodious sounds; praise with the sublime song of Vajra-gīti,
then proceed with vigor as the two hands join in the hollow-heart gesture.
Bend the fingers so that their backs touch, thereby forming the *mudrā* of the Mother.
Recite the mantra for the peaceful intention seven times;
protect the *maṇi* of the tutelary deity by coiling it within the palms joined together, and recite the Great Heart Mantra seven times.
The Wisdom [finger] is joined with the Tranquility [finger], And the Meditation and Precept [fingers] are likewise;
The remaining *pāramitās* are all extended straight. The Effort [finger] is joined at the back of the Patience [finger], While the Strength [finger] is attached to the top of the Vow [finger].
The two circles are used to support the bead.
Having contemplated within one's own mind, as clearly manifest as the full moon,
and having dwelt in clear observation,
one should bring forth from the mouth the secret mantra of the Mother of the Family, the Vidyā.
Each syllable is golden in color, universally emitting immeasurable light that follows one another like a string of pearls. As they enter the mouths of oneself and others,
they scatter upon the lunar mandalas and transform in color according to the respective deities.
The flame-crested [deity] pierces through the causal signs; the words and phrases are without error.
The practitioner possesses a majestic and heroic appearance; reciting the secret mantra, he takes refuge in "Oṃ," which is entirely quiescent.
As for the remaining syllables, they are uttered with a fierce and wrathful mind.
When the syllable *ma* is reached, one should grasp the single bead so that it aligns with the mantra;
abiding in this gate of samādhi, one should maintain the recitation with all one's strength.
When the practice is about to cease, one should join the beads together within the palms.
As before, perform the empowerment once more; placing [the deity] upon the crown of the head, return it to its original place.
Dwell for a moment in quiet contemplation, and carefully consider the true nature of the mantra’s meaning, principles, and phrasing within the lunar disc.
Next, having emerged from meditative absorption, golden light from the mantra issues from one's mouth like a string of pearls.
One should pay homage at the station of the Mother of the Family and make this aspiration: "May you sustain this mantra."
Through the protection of compassion, may no loss of the efficacy of the recitation count occur;
recite the mantra of the Family Mother seven times to provide protection,
and one should perform the rite in this manner.
All classes of sentient beings, their bodies oppressed by various sufferings and afflictions,
are not yet fit vessels for enlightenment; therefore,
I shall deliver them, and not merely extract myself alone from suffering.
I pray only that the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
may accomplish the return-counting of the mudrās of the three families; then, as before,
perform the sequence of the first [rite] to protect the body of the tutelary deity, using the seal of the Mother of the preceding family.
Holding the left *argha* vessel, present it as an offering while articulating one's requests;
the ritual procedure is no different from what precedes.
Next, perform the mental offering to the fire mandala with the *Guhyasandhi-mudrā*, releasing it over the head on the left side.
Release all mudrās; one should then perform the seal for escorting the assembly of sages to descend into the maṇḍala.
With the wisdom-pāramitā mudrā, snap the fingers outward and again form the seal for inviting the celestial chariot; the assembly of sages shall ascend upon it.
Abandoning meditative concentration and wisdom externally, return the visualization to the fundamental palace.
As before, protect your own body; then, outside the site of practice, seal it with the mudrā of the stūpa and recite the *Vaipulya Mahāyāna Sūtra* according to your inclination.
Dedicate this to assist in the prayers of the mouth; may the *siddhis* of the superior, middling, and inferior levels be attained.
When going to places of defilement, clench the wings of wisdom into fists and extend the fingers of dhyāna-pāramitā like mountain peaks;
thus protect the body by applying [the mudrās] to the five locations.
When employing mantras, one should use the *añjali-mudrā* (clasped hands gesture);
thus it is universally taught that one will not be overcome by the māras. One should apply the mind [to the rite] and especially offer food and drink;
whatever is available may be arranged as an offering. Use the Great Mind Mantra (*mahācitta-mantra*).
When wishing to remove withered flowers, recite this secret mantra:
"If one wishes to sleep, one should protect the body with the Family Mother (Kulamātṛ) and protect the location with the Family Lord (Kulapati) mudrā and mantra."
As before, perform the descent-entrance mudrā; press forward with the Prajñāpāramitā [mudrā] while reciting the subsequent mantra.
To awaken the deities, one should purify oneself of seminal emission and bad dreams by reciting the Kuleśvarī-vidyā one hundred times.
Whenever one wishes to eat, place the food in that spot;
with the mantra that provides protection, offer it before the principal deity of the family,
and having consecrated the food with the mantra, then eat.
Next, one should explain the four subtle ritual manuals that ought to be practiced:
Śāntika for pacifying calamities, as well as the methods for attaining intelligence, longevity, and the removal of enmity and misfortune;
[in these,] one should sit facing north with the legs crossed.
With knees upright and the right shin forward, one's clothing should be pure white;
food, drink, incense, flowers, and the ground, as well as the lamps and candles, should likewise be so.
One should arrange the mantra upon a moon disc, and the syllables should also be white.
First, recite the homage in unison; after twenty-one repetitions, the [obstacles] will be removed.
Begin with *Oṃ*, and end with *svāhā* followed by "remove the calamities for [Name].
This is the original form; do not add anything when performing the rite.
One should recite with a low voice, maintaining a tranquil mind.
If one constructs a great maṇḍala, the hearth should be circular and perforated;
within it, one should fashion a wheel, and the protective deity should be depicted with a fierce and wrathful aspect.
If one seeks increase, it is called pauṣṭika;
through the five supernatural powers and the wheel-turning [king], the treasure-vase, the wheel, the sword, and the vajra,
one attains all wealth and possessions, including medicinal pills and eye-salve.
Facing east, sit in the full lotus posture; their color is entirely deep red.
Recite the mantra phrases with appropriate additions or omissions as before, without any further variation;
if you wish to append "svāhā," do so, and that which is sought will be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
With a low voice and a tranquil mind, one should protect the wrathful and fierce Honored One by constructing a square altar and drilling a hearth;
there, one should place a trident-topped ritual dagger (*kīla*).
If one seeks the method for rousing passion, it is called *Vaśyākarṣaṇa*.
Summoning humans, devas, nāgas, spirits, and those who are not human, facing west and seated in the half-lotus posture;
the ritual for increasing [the power] of the Red [deity], including the additions and subtractions, and the text for taking refuge: *svāhā* is likewise applied.
Together with [Name], I shall gather [Name].
May the Vidyādhara who fulfills all aspirations be joyful;
may the Protector with a peaceful mind and likewise with a fierce aspect protect both in two ways.
The hearth is like an eight-petaled lotus, fully blossomed with its pedestal and filaments.
If one performs the rite of subjugation (*abhicāruka*)—
to suppress ghosts, spirits, and evil persons who destroy the Triple Gem— [one should visualize it thus].
Pressing the right [toe] with the left toe, sitting in a squatting posture facing west, one assumes a form of great wrath.
Visualize all colors as dark blue-black above, with a luminous circle at the heart;
transform this into the great solar disc.
Blazing and peerless, emitting radiance like a fierce flame, remove [obstacles] with *svāhā*.
"May [this] be accomplished for [so-and-so] for such-and-such a purpose," *hūṃ*—thus resolve the mind. Construct the fire pit as a triangle.
Place a single-pronged pestle in the center; recite the mantra with fierce intensity as if a bystander were listening.
Next, one should set forth the ritual procedures for the peaceful mind of the protective deity, and accordingly place the primary deity therein.
The center is the location for the hearth; alternatively, outside the sanctum, the hearth may be positioned at a distance directly facing the Honored One.
The ground should be prepared over an area of two cubits, its shape following the contour of the hearth's opening, with steps built one finger-width high.
The medium-sized [fire pit] is one cubit (*hasta*) in diameter; it is completed as a hearth with a depth of half a cubit.
Its rim is four finger-widths high, and one *aṅgula* (finger-width) outside this, the square shape of the hearth is formed according to the Dharma. The wheel and vajra are made of clay.
Place it in the center and weigh its base; smear it with *gomaya* and adorn it with sandalwood and the like.
Furthermore, provide for its color according to what is sought;
on the steps, place auspicious *kuśa* grass, arranged in a clockwise circle following the direction of the sun.
Cover the seedlings with their original [sheaths]; the objects to be burned shall be placed near the grass on the right side of the path.
Place two vessels of *argha* water upon the grass by the side of the door;
the firewood should follow, pushed along the cheeks.
Cut ten fingers' length from a long stick; dip both ends of the wood into ghee, honey, milk, and curd.
Cast them into a brazier filled with glowing coals, and they will likewise ignite with fierce flames;
do not use old fire-sticks for this purpose.
Use a fan rather than blowing with the mouth; when kindling the brazier, recite the mantra after the fire has already begun to emit light and flames.
One should employ the Wrathful King to cast out impurities and purify them;
the secret mudrā is to be bound in this manner.
The two palms are joined back-to-back; eight times they are rotated like a hook, with the wrists reversed to join together.
Forming fists, one seals all objects, reciting the mantra each time upon contact. Following this is the secret mantra.
Furthermore, one should invite the Fire Deity (*Agnideva*).
Extend the "wisdom-feather" (*prajñā-pakṣa*) straight and cross the "meditation-hand" (*dhyāna-hasta*) over the palm; with the "progressive step" (*vīrya-pada*), beckon slightly.
Recite the subsequent mantra three times for each beckoning, and the Fire Deity will descend.
Then, visualize entering the hearth; next, bind the *samaya* mudrā and perform the initial *tāṇḍava* gesture of the *dāna-pāramitā*.
Extend the remaining *pāramitās* and sprinkle *argha* water directly; thus, purification is accomplished within the fire.
Recite the vidyā-mantra three times for the sprinkling; then,
with the right hand acting as a "wisdom-feather" (*prajñā-pakṣa*), perform the clockwise sprinkling of the arghya while reciting the Mañjuśrī-secret-mantra,
visualizing that it rinses the mouth of the deity Agni.
The large ladle is fixed as the feather-hand; the small one is wisdom, which should be held.
Three times take the name-soma and pour it until the large ladle is full.
Wisdom abandons the small and grasps the large; there is a sword and so forth to press down upon it.
Next, recite the mantra; at the end of each phrase, visualize the fire being poured upon it.
Whenever you reach the syllable *ha*, draw out the sound with a long resonance, then withdraw the empty ladle and press it down; thus the sound shall conclude evenly.
Do not add sword-shaped ladles or medicinal substances; simply pour [the water] without pressing the ladle.
This is the ritual for sacrificing to the Fire Deity.
Perform this three times in the same manner, then purify the fire again as before. Use the Mañjuśrī mantra for rinsing the mouth.
Please the Fire Deity to emerge from the furnace and take his place in the southeast;
there, one should arrange all the offerings. Next, invite the Lord of the Family, who dwells afar, into the center of the furnace;
visualize him clearly as he abides according to his position.
Furthermore, visualize the tutelary deity entering the fire pit, positioned near the practitioner and corresponding with the Lord of the Family.
The two sages stand solemnly face-to-face;
the Wrathful King pours away impurities, and the pure fire rinses the mouth with clarity.
Perform it again according to the Dharma: Place both hands between the knees as in the previous fire-offering ritual.
Offer three ladles of clarified butter each time, while first visualizing oneself as the Principal Deity and the Lord of the Family.
Fire, swords, medicinal herbs, and so forth—these all share one single characteristic without distinction.
Since the five limbs are thus unified, offer each with its own *vidyā-mantra*.
Having performed such offerings in this manner, perform the *homa* according to the specific purpose sought.
Observe what is required for the burning: whether a ladle is appropriate or the hand should be used.
If a ladle-like implement is needed, take the smaller one previously mentioned;
having poured [the liquid], proceed with a steady gait, extending it so that it remains aligned with its handle.
With dāna, śīla, kṣānti, and so forth, together with dhyānapāramitā,
take the first mudrā and rotate the beads; reciting once for each bead,
cast them into the fire until the count is complete, then offer the beads back as before.
The two sages return to the altar. Again, having recited the *Agnideva-homa* and completed the three large ladles of clarified butter (*ghṛta*), they take their seats as at the beginning.
If it is necessary to perform offerings to the eight directions, one should invite [the deities] for each one.
Dissolve the boundary according to the ritual procedure and dispatch [the deity].
Next, arrange the fire-deity mudrā as previously described during the time of invocation.
Press the fingers together in the *dhyāna-mudrā* and recite the mantra once more; then the fire-deity returns to his palace.
As previously protected by oneself, one will no longer be disturbed by the various māras.
One will dream of Buddhas and bodhisattvas, vajra-holding celestial kings,
brahmins, and householders, partaking of fine rice and curd-rice.
Amṛta, milk, fruit, and flowers; flourishing forests as if ascending a mountain;
walking upon stupas and multi-storied pavilions; or riding in chariots, on horses, elephants, white cranes, or peacock kings; together with the garuḍa.
Pervading the sea and clear flowing waters, Or soaring through the air with sovereign majesty,
Flames pervading the entire body, Or listening within the Dharma seat and amidst all pure matters— These are all signs of accomplishment.
How much more so now—do not sleep again! If in a dream you see a butcher, a pig, a donkey, a camel, or a dog;
or if you touch a corpse, or even come near one—the same applies:
it is merely the terror of evil spirits.
This is an obstruction, not a sign. Should any deluded thoughts arise that violate or omit the samaya,
one should recite this mantra to eliminate those faults and afflictions,
as previously described for the vajra.
The advancing forces join together; the patience and vows rely upon the armor, encircling and supporting one another from above.
Recite the mantra as follows twenty-one times, and all obstacles will be eliminated.
The mantra of the Great Wheel is as follows:
Whenever performing visualization, close your eyes and concentrate the mind until the image is clearly manifest;
then, with eyes open, behold that you have become the World-Protecting Deities of the Eight Directions. The mantra is as follows:
The King Maheśvara resides in the northeastern corner;
his mantra is recited as follows: *Oṃ rudrāya svāhā*.
This is the mantra for the position of Indra in the east, honored by all the devas. It is said: *Oṃ rudrāya svāhā*.
Oṃ śakrāya svāhā. The mantra for the deity Agni in the southeast is: Oṃ agnaye svāhā.
The mantra for the position of the deity Yama in the south is: [Oṃ yamāya svāhā].
Oṃ vīvasvate svāhā. The mantra of the Lord of the Southwest is: Oṃ rākṣasādhipataye svāhā.
The mantra for the position of Varuṇa in the West is: Oṃ varuṇāya svāhā.
Oṃ miṅgaśanaye svāhā. The mantra for the position of Vāyu (Wind Deity) in the northwest is:
Oṃ vāyave svāhā. The mantra for Vaiśravaṇa Deva in the north is: Oṃ vaiśravaṇāya svāhā.
One should invite the honored ones of the eight directions and those who are to be venerated,
performing all matters according to their respective wishes;
for the construction of maṇḍalas and the performance of all ritual activities, one should always employ the root mantras.
Having first offered all manner of sustenance— food, drink, incense, lamps, bright offerings,
argha water, flowers, and unguents— arranging these objects in every direction,
may there be no obstacles whatsoever, and may all aspirations be fulfilled according to one's heart.
For both the principal deity and the lord of the family, the original mantra should be used;
as for the sequence previously described as "winding and tossing," it should be revised to "winding and wheeling."
Furthermore, in the section on the mantra methods for beginners in the lower fascicle, it was previously stated:
"If one obtains *māra* leaves, one obtains the title of *bhoga*;
as for *dhūrasaka*, it is *sahakāra* (sandalwood)."
Mix powdered [incense] with mustard seeds and offer them into the fire one thousand and eight times;
this will cause all people to revere the practitioner of the mantra.
Please change this to: "If one takes the powder of *jintongxiang* (Cinnamomum tamala) and *tianzhusuhexiang* (Styrax benzoin),
mixes them with mustard oil,
and offers them into the fire one thousand and eight times."
It should be noted that four lines have been omitted from the ancient version of the *Rénlín fúdé yí* (The Ritual for Bestowing Merit upon People).
They are as follows: "Upon all forms, blue and black;
within the mind, gradually becoming round and luminous."
It transforms into the great sun-disk,
blazing and peerless,
radiating brilliance like a fierce flame.
One fascicle of the Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the Greatly Majestic and Wrathful Ucchuṣma.
